dossier.purpose: Git (git/git), the distributed version control system, read for two built-in capabilities: `git worktree` (linked working trees sharing one repository: add/list/lock/unlock/move/remove/prune/repair; builtin/worktree.c, worktree.c) and `git diff` including `--no-index` (compare two filesystem paths with or without a repository; diff-no-index.c, builtin/diff.c) on the xdiff engine plus regex-based language drivers (userdiff.c). The 75-line README says nothing about worktrees, --no-index, GitHub/PR automation, structural diffs, MCP or agents; those facts come from Documentation/ and the code. Findings relevant to the needs: Git is the VCS base with native worktrees and line/word-level diffs; the tree has no GitHub API client, no PR/review/mention-triggered automation (its .github/workflows are Git's own CI plus an l10n lint that comments on PRs), no CI-status or merge feature in `git worktree`, and no parser-based or entity-level diff. The snapshot is a development revision after v2.56 (GIT-VERSION-GEN:3 fallback v2.56.GIT; in-progress release notes are Documentation/RelNotes/2.98.0.adoc). Method: static reading only (no shell available); nothing was built, run or tested.

claims.claim: Git is a fast, scalable, distributed revision control system with an unusually rich command set that provides both high-level operations and full access to internals.
Open source under the GNU GPL version 2; some parts are under different licenses compatible with GPLv2.
Originally written by Linus Torvalds with help of a group of hackers around the net.
Installation instructions are in the file INSTALL.
Docs: start with Documentation/gittutorial.adoc, then giteveryday.adoc, and Documentation/git-<commandname>.adoc per command; once installed, `man git-<commandname>` or `git help <commandname>`.
User discussion and development take place on the Git mailing list (git@vger.kernel.org): bug reports, feature requests, comments and patches go there.
Mailing-list archives are at lore.kernel.org/git and marc.info; subscribe via git+subscribe@vger.kernel.org.
Security-relevant issues are to be disclosed privately to git-security@googlegroups.com.
The maintainer's frequent 'What's cooking' reports list the status of development topics and are a good reference for project status, direction and remaining tasks.
Localization (l10n) of messages is coordinated via po/README.md.
CI status badges for the GitHub Actions 'CI' workflow and a GitLab pipeline on master.
Absence: the README does not mention git worktree, git diff --no-index, GitHub/PR automation, structural or syntax-aware diffs, MCP, AI agents, telemetry or supported platforms.

install.method: GNU make from source (Linux/macOS; INSTALL has no macOS-specific section)
install.command: make prefix=/usr all doc info   # then, as root: make prefix=/usr install install-doc install-html install-info   (plain `make` + `make install` installs under ~/bin)
make configure ; ./configure --prefix=/usr ; make all doc ; (as root) make install install-doc install-html

install.method: Meson + Ninja (documented in the meson.build header, not in INSTALL)
install.command: meson setup build/ ; then inside build/: meson compile ; meson test ; meson install
make prefix=/usr profile ; make prefix=/usr PROFILE=BUILD install   (faster training variant: make prefix=/usr profile-fast ; make prefix=/usr PROFILE=BUILD install)

integrations.cli: The `git` binary is the product: `git worktree` (git.c:687 -> builtin/worktree.c:1512), `git diff` (git.c:571 -> builtin/diff.c:399; --no-index -> diff-no-index.c:354) and `git difftool` (git.c:576 -> builtin/difftool.c:717). Script-friendly output: `git worktree list --porcelain [-z]` (Documentation/git-worktree.adoc:259-269, 460-511); `git diff --raw/--numstat/--name-status/-z` and `--word-diff=porcelain` (Documentation/diff-options.adoc:149,231,305-330,447-453); `diff --no-index` exit codes 0/1 (t/t4053-diff-no-index.sh:19-22).
integrations.mcp: none found - no 'Model Context Protocol' or MCP server references anywhere in the tree (all files searched).
integrations.sdk_or_api: No supported SDK or HTTP API. Internal static library libgit.a (Makefile:941); proof-of-concept Rust FFI crates in contrib/ (contrib/libgit-rs/README.md:3; contrib/libgit-sys/README.md:3-4); the stable programmatic surface is the CLI above. Trace2 JSON events are diagnostic output (Documentation/technical/api-trace2.adoc:104-109). No GitHub API client exists in the C, shell, Perl or Python sources (GitHub appears there only as URLs in comments, e.g. builtin/push.c:790).
integrations.claude_code_or_codex: none found for Claude Code or Codex (no CLAUDE.md; no matches for 'claude code' or 'codex'). Related: po/AGENTS.md:1-5 is an optional instruction file for 'AI agents' doing localization housekeeping (referenced at po/README.md:402-414), and Documentation/SubmittingPatches:571-597 sets an AI-use policy for contributions.

readme.telemetry_and_network: No telemetry or phone-home code found. The only 'telemetry' hits are the optional Trace2 facility (trace2.h:5; Documentation/technical/api-trace2.adoc:3-5): inactive unless explicitly enabled, read only from system/global config and GIT_TRACE2* env (api-trace2.adoc:4-5,25-28); sinks are stderr, fds, files/directories or AF_UNIX sockets (Documentation/trace2-target-values.adoc:2-11; trace2/tr2_dst.c:199-285), no network sink. git fast-import writes local crash reports (Documentation/git-fast-import.adoc:1348-1352). Network is used by transport commands (ssh, and HTTP(S) via libcurl: INSTALL:117,132-139); `git worktree` and `git diff --no-index` operate on the local filesystem (builtin/worktree.c, diff-no-index.c), but in partial clones diff/checkout can lazily fetch missing objects from the promisor remote (Documentation/technical/partial-clone.adoc:125-134; t/t4067-diff-partial-clone.sh). Outbound identification: HTTP User-Agent 'git/<version>' (http.c:1255-1256; override via http.userAgent / GIT_HTTP_USER_AGENT, http.c:502-503,1475; build option meson_options.txt:34-35) and the protocol 'agent=' capability (send-pack.c:599, fetch-pack.c:418). ident.c:103-145 may resolve the local hostname via getaddrinfo when deriving a default identity. No account or hosted service is required; remote authentication uses credential helpers, including PAT/OAuth via third-party helpers (Documentation/gitcredentials.adoc:21,116-134). CI-only network use: coverity.yml uploads to scan.coverity.com when enabled (coverity.yml:22-31,160-167); l10n.yml installs git-po-helper from GitHub (l10n.yml:70-71).

entry_points.what: main(): calls cmd_main() (common-main.c:9) for git and every helper program.
cmd_main of the `git` binary: command-table dispatch, incl. { "diff", cmd_diff } at git.c:571 and { "worktree", cmd_worktree } at git.c:687.
cmd_worktree: subcommands add, prune, list, lock, unlock, move, remove, repair (OPT_SUBCOMMAND table at :1518-1528).
cmd_diff: decides explicit/implicit --no-index (:446-477), otherwise index/tree/blob diffs.
diff_no_index(): filesystem-vs-filesystem diff; '-' reads stdin, directories recurse, pathspecs only when both paths are directories.
cmd_main of the HTTP(S) remote-transport helper program.
Further cmd_main programs: daemon.c:1258, http-backend.c:764, shell.c:161, imap-send.c:1804, http-fetch.c:98, http-push.c:1716, scalar.c:1016.

code.architecture: Single C code base producing the `git` binary (130 builtin/*.c files) plus helper programs. Flow: common-main.c main -> git.c cmd_main (command table) -> builtin/*.c. Worktrees: CLI and validation in builtin/worktree.c (runs the post-checkout hook, :610-622; spawns `git branch` for new branches, :981-995; spawns `git status --porcelain` for the cleanliness check, :1390-1393); model/prune/repair logic in worktree.c; per-worktree admin dirs under $GIT_COMMON_DIR/worktrees/<id>/ (Documentation/git-worktree.adoc:363-393) with a per-worktree ref store (builtin/worktree.c:549-565). Diff: builtin/diff.c picks the mode -> diff-lib.c (index/working-tree comparison helpers) or diff-no-index.c (filesystem walk, stdin/pipe support) -> diffcore-*.c stages (rename, break, pickaxe, order; diff.c:7463 diffcore_std) -> diff.c (patch/stat/raw output, word diff, --color-moved, external diff, textconv; diff_flush at :7166) -> xdiff/ (LibXDiff-derived engine: Myers/minimal, patience, histogram in xdiffi.c, xpatience.c, xhistogram.c; hunk and funcname emission in xemit.c). Per-language regex drivers live in userdiff.c and are selected through the `diff` gitattribute (diff.c:2308-2321). Storage and refs: odb/*.c, object-file.c, packfile.c; refs/{files,packed,reftable}-backend.c and reftable/. Network: transport.c, http.c, remote-curl.c. Diagnostics: trace2/. Portability: compat/. Optional Rust staticlib `gitcore` from src/*.rs (Cargo.toml) and proof-of-concept bindings in contrib/libgit-{sys,rs}. Scripts: git-*.sh, *.perl, git-p4.py. GUIs: git-gui/, gitk-git/. Tests: t/.
code.packaging_and_release: No release-publishing workflow exists among the five GitHub workflows, .gitlab-ci.yml or .cirrus.yml. Source tarball: `make dist` (git archive -> git-<ver>.tar.gz, adds `configure` and a `version` file; Makefile:3798-3826) or `meson dist` (meson.build:2354-2365); doc tarballs via `make dist-doc` (Makefile:3847-3850). Version string: `version` file in tarballs, else `git describe`, else DEF_VER (GIT-VERSION-GEN:40-61). Release train: feature releases vX.Y.0 every 8-10 weeks, maintenance vX.Y.Z; branches master/maint/next/seen (Documentation/howto/maintain-git.adoc:35-133). Release tags are signed by the maintainer's GPG key (Documentation/howto/coordinate-embargoed-releases.adoc:198-199). No checksums, signatures or provenance attestations are generated by any workflow, the Makefile or meson.build (searched, none found); upload-artifact is used only for CI test hand-off and failure dumps (.github/workflows/main.yml:152,186,237,273,299,334,378,480).
code.tests_and_ci: Frameworks: (1) POSIX-shell TAP integration tests t/t[0-9]{4}-*.sh, 1,061 files, run by `make test`, `prove` or `meson test` (t/README:14-64; meson.build:50-81); (2) C unit tests on the vendored clar framework in t/unit-tests/ (28 u-*.c files incl. 8 reftable suites, plus lib/runner files; Makefile:4080); (3) perf suite t/perf/ (65 p*.sh incl. p4000-diff-algorithms, p4001-diff-no-index, p4002-diff-color-moved); (4) oss-fuzz/ fuzzers (9 fuzz-*.c, smoke-run in CI); (5) about 80 helper programs t/helper/test-*.c. Relevant suites: worktree t2400-t2407 (8 files, 225 test cases: add 91, prune 13, list 27, move 33, config 12, submodule 11, repair 26, heads 12); diff t4000-t4074 (75 files) incl. t4053-diff-no-index.sh (41 cases), t4018-diff-funcname.sh with 210 fixture files in t/t4018/, t4034-diff-words.sh with 60 fixture files for 20 languages in t/t4034/, t4051-diff-function-context.sh, t4020-diff-external.sh, t4030-diff-textconv.sh, t4065-diff-anchored.sh. CI: .github/workflows/main.yml (push + pull_request; jobs: config, Windows build/test in 10 slices, Windows+VS for the git-for-windows owner only, Windows+Meson, 4 macOS jobs on macos-14, fuzz smoke, 13 Linux container jobs incl. sha256, reftable, asan/ubsan, leaks, musl/Alpine, 32-bit, AlmaLinux 8, Debian 12, Fedora, breaking-changes, static analysis with Coccinelle/header/pot checks, Rust fmt/clippy/msrv, sparse, docs build); check-style.yml (git clang-format on PRs, continue-on-error); check-whitespace.yml (git log --check on PRs); coverity.yml (opt-in via repo variables); l10n.yml (git-po-helper for l10n repos/branches, comments on PRs). Also .gitlab-ci.yml (Linux, macOS, Windows, fuzz, static analysis, Rust, whitespace, style, docs) and .cirrus.yml (FreeBSD 14.3: gmake test unit-tests). Nothing was executed for this dossier.
code.dependencies: Cargo.toml (root crate gitcore, staticlib): 0 dependencies (Cargo.toml:10-11). contrib/libgit-sys/Cargo.toml: 1 dependency (libz-sys) + 2 build-deps (autocfg, make-cmd), Cargo.lock lists 9 packages. contrib/libgit-rs/Cargo.toml: 1 dependency (libgit-sys, path) + 1 build-dep (autocfg), Cargo.lock lists 10 packages. meson.build performs 15 dependency() lookups over 14 distinct packages (zlib-ng/zlib, threads, intl, iconv, libpcre2-8, libcurl, expat, openssl, nettle, gcrypt, macOS frameworks; meson.build:991-1677), needs Meson >=0.61.0 (meson.build:224); only zlib is mandatory, the rest optional (INSTALL:110-162). subprojects/*.wrap: 5 fallback wraps (curl, expat, openssl, pcre2, zlib). .gitmodules: 1 submodule (sha1collisiondetection) with an in-tree copy in sha1dc/. Optional runtime tools: Perl >=5.26, Python 3 (git-p4), Tcl/Tk (gitk, git-gui), asciidoc/asciidoctor + xmlto for docs. No package.json, go.mod, pyproject.toml or requirements files.
code.security_policy: SECURITY.md - private reports to git-security@googlegroups.com (SECURITY.md:3-6); no LTS versions, fixes target the latest maintenance track and merge upward (SECURITY.md:29-42).

claim_checks.evidence: The README gives no numbers. The tree has a perf harness (t/perf/: 65 p*.sh scripts incl. p4000-diff-algorithms.sh, p4001-diff-no-index.sh, p4002-diff-color-moved.sh; meson_options.txt:122-129) but publishes no results, only qualitative statements (INSTALL:34-37; Documentation/BreakingChanges.adoc:150-153). Nothing was run.

claim_checks.claim: A distributed system with full access to internals (README.md:7-9).
claim_checks.evidence: Distribution builtins exist (builtin/clone.c, fetch.c, push.c, pull.c); plumbing is exposed in the command table (git.c:572-575: diff-files, diff-index, diff-tree).

claim_checks.claim: GPLv2 project with some parts under other GPLv2-compatible licenses (README.md:11-13).
claim_checks.evidence: COPYING:1-4,22-27 is GPL v2 only ('not v2.2 or v3.x'). Mixed parts: xdiff LGPL-2.1-or-later (xdiff/xdiff.h:5-9), reftable BSD-style (reftable/basics.c:2-6), sha1dc MIT (sha1dc/LICENSE.txt:1), clar ISC (t/unit-tests/clar/COPYING:1).

claim_checks.claim: INSTALL is the place for installation instructions (README.md:16).
claim_checks.evidence: INSTALL:4-26 covers make and autoconf only; Meson is documented in meson.build:1-97, not INSTALL. INSTALL's dependency list (INSTALL:110-162) omits Rust/Cargo although Makefile:488-497,943-956 and meson_options.txt:84-85 enable Rust by default (Documentation/BreakingChanges.adoc:190-198: builds break by default if Rust is missing). INSTALL:137 says libcurl >= 7.61.0 while meson.build:1164 requires >= 7.21.3. The build files take precedence.

claim_checks.claim: Security issues go privately to git-security@googlegroups.com (README.md:48-49).
claim_checks.evidence: SECURITY.md:3-6 repeats the address; SECURITY.md:29-42 adds that there is no LTS and fixes go to the newest maintenance track.

claim_checks.claim: Development happens on the mailing list (README.md:33-37); GitHub is not the contribution channel (.github/CONTRIBUTING.md:3-9).
claim_checks.evidence: .github/CONTRIBUTING.md:3-9 and .github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md:1-5 say github.com is not used for contributions; GitGitGadget (external) turns PRs into mails (Documentation/MyFirstContribution.adoc:860-866). In-tree workflows are CI/lint only (main.yml, check-style.yml, check-whitespace.yml, coverity.yml, l10n.yml); the sole PR-commenting job is l10n.yml:94-111 (git-po-helper lint, not an agent, not mention-triggered).

claim_checks.claim: `git diff --no-index` compares two filesystem paths, may omit the option outside a repo or when a path is outside the working tree, and implies --exit-code (Documentation/git-diff.adoc:34-45).
claim_checks.evidence: builtin/diff.c:446-477: explicit flag; implicit when outside a repo or when exactly two path arguments are given and either is outside the repo (the 'exactly two' restriction is not in the docs). diff-no-index.c:420 sets exit_with_status; t/t4053-diff-no-index.sh:19-22,46-50 assert exit codes 0/1.

claim_checks.claim: `git worktree list --porcelain` output is stable and scriptable (Documentation/git-worktree.adoc:259-263).
claim_checks.evidence: builtin/worktree.c:1010-1041 emits the documented keys (worktree, bare, HEAD, detached, branch, locked [reason], prunable [reason]); -z at :1139-1140; --verbose with --porcelain is rejected at :1148-1149; covered by t/t2402-worktree-list.sh (cases starting at :63,78,93,108,125,150). The promise of future stability is a policy statement and not checkable in code.

claim_checks.claim: Native worktree tooling can list worktrees with CI status and merge them (implied by the needs, not claimed by the docs).
claim_checks.evidence: Only eight subcommands exist (builtin/worktree.c:1518-1528: add, prune, list, lock, unlock, move, remove, repair). list prints path, abbreviated HEAD, branch/detached/bare, locked, prunable (builtin/worktree.c:1010-1086); 'prunable' is purely metadata-based (worktree.c:937-1029). `remove` deletes only the worktree and its admin dir, not the branch (builtin/worktree.c:1463-1474). Merge and branch cleanup are separate commands: git merge, git merge-tree --write-tree (Documentation/git-merge-tree.adoc:6,24-25) and git branch --delete-merged, which skips branches checked out in any worktree (Documentation/git-branch.adoc:205-221).

claim_checks.claim: Git offers syntax-aware diffs through built-in language drivers and word diff (Documentation/gitattributes.adoc:861-939; Documentation/diff-options.adoc:435-467).
claim_checks.evidence: The drivers are regexes (userdiff.c:36-44, 45-377): funcname patterns drive hunk headers, -W function context (diff.c:4039-4043) and -L :funcname (Documentation/line-range-format.adoc:25-32); word diff re-diffs regex-split words inside line-diff hunks (diff.c:2191-2263; diff-options.adoc:461-467). The code has 28 drivers while gitattributes.adoc:867-919 lists 26 (ini, userdiff.c:224, and r, userdiff.c:330, are undocumented); the code is authoritative. No parser, tree-sitter, entity-level or 'structural diff' code exists (no matches anywhere in the tree). External viewers plug in via diff.external/GIT_EXTERNAL_DIFF (diff.c:558-574), diff.<driver>.command (userdiff.c:491-494) and git difftool -x (Documentation/git-difftool.adoc:90-91).

benchmarks.what: Profile-feedback (PGO) build of Git versus a normal build

benchmarks.value: unquantified: 'significantly outperforms ... by multiple orders of magnitude'

risks: Scope: nothing for GitHub automation. The tree has no GitHub API client, PR/check/review tooling or mention-triggered agent automation; GitHub appears in C/shell/Python only as comment URLs (builtin/push.c:790). The project does not use github.com for contributions (.github/CONTRIBUTING.md:3-9); its five workflows are Git's own CI and lint (.github/workflows/*.yml) and the only PR-commenting job is the l10n lint (l10n.yml:94-111).

Scope: `git worktree` has no CI-status, merge or branch-removal feature (builtin/worktree.c:1518-1528, 1463-1474). 'prunable' reflects missing or stale metadata only (worktree.c:937-1029); `remove` refuses dirty or locked worktrees, and worktrees with submodules without --force (builtin/worktree.c:1372-1409, 1450-1466).

Parallel-agent constraints: one worktree per branch unless forced (Documentation/git-worktree.adoc:180-185; builtin/worktree.c:485-486,901-904). Docs call multiple checkout 'still experimental', with incomplete submodule support and a recommendation against multiple checkouts of a superproject (git-worktree.adoc:540-544). worktree.useRelativePaths and extensions.worktreeConfig make a repository unreadable to older Git (Documentation/config/worktree.adoc:18-20; git-worktree.adoc:344-345). Repository config is shared across worktrees unless worktreeConfig is enabled (git-worktree.adoc:330-336). Orphaned admin files are pruned by git gc only after gc.worktreePruneExpire, default 3 months (Documentation/config/gc.adoc:107-111).

Diff scope: line-based diff with regex language drivers, no parser or entity-level diff (userdiff.c:36-44; no tree-sitter, 'entity-level' or 'structural diff' matches in the tree). Word diff 'may produce a larger diff than a dedicated word-diff tool' (Documentation/diff-options.adoc:461-467). By code reading (not executed), `git diff --no-index` exits 1 both for 'differences found' and for access errors: diff_no_index starts with ret = 1 and jumps to cleanup when queue_diff fails (diff-no-index.c:360,422-424; error text at :95), so scripts cannot tell the cases apart from the status alone. Pathspecs are rejected unless both paths are directories (diff-no-index.c:394-404).

Build and platform: Rust is compiled by default unless NO_RUST or -Drust=disabled (Makefile:488-497,943-956; meson_options.txt:84-85) and becomes mandatory in Git 3.0 (Documentation/BreakingChanges.adoc:174-217); INSTALL's dependency list does not mention Rust/Cargo or Meson (INSTALL:110-162); INSTALL and meson.build disagree on the libcurl minimum (INSTALL:137 vs meson.build:1164). WSL2 support is not stated anywhere in the tree.

Version churn: this is a development snapshot between releases. GIT-VERSION-GEN:3 falls back to v2.56.GIT and this shallow clone has no tags, so `git describe` cannot name the version (GIT-VERSION-GEN:45-58); the in-progress notes are Documentation/RelNotes/2.98.0.adoc, which calls it the 'antepenultimate release' before Git 3.0 (:4-5). Git 3.0 has no release date but plans default changes: sha256 object format, reftable ref storage, `main` branch name, safe.bareRepository=explicit (Documentation/BreakingChanges.adoc:82-241); breaking changes are guarded by WITH_BREAKING_CHANGES (:72-77).

Maintenance and security: no LTS; only the latest maintenance track is formally patched (SECURITY.md:31-42); a feature release every 8-10 weeks (Documentation/howto/maintain-git.adoc:111-115). No release workflow, checksums or attestations exist in .github/, .gitlab-ci.yml, .cirrus.yml, the Makefile or meson.build (searched); the only signature evidence is maintainer-signed tags (Documentation/howto/coordinate-embargoed-releases.adoc:198-199). contrib/ (diff-highlight, credential helpers, libgit-rs) is owner-maintained and not actively reviewed by the maintainer (contrib/README:10-21); libgit-rs and libgit-sys are proof-of-concept and their Cargo manifests carry no license field.

License and contribution policy: GPL-2.0-only, 'v2, not v2.2 or v3.x' (COPYING:2-4), with mixed-license components (xdiff LGPL-2.1+, reftable BSD-style, sha1dc MIT, clar ISC). Upstream contribution policy rejects 'anything that looks AI generated' (Documentation/SubmittingPatches:584-587) and takes patches by mailing list, GitGitGadget or b4 (SubmittingPatches:673; .github/CONTRIBUTING.md:3-9).
